recognize_zh: 周邊血液中增加的中小型淋巴球，細胞質深藍且常有突起或泡狀邊緣（cytoplasmic blebs），細胞核略不規則，符合 T 細胞前淋巴球性白血病（T-PLL）。
features: Increased small to medium-sized atypical lymphoid cells
Deeply basophilic, agranular cytoplasm with irregular protrusions/blebs
Round to irregular nuclei with moderately condensed chromatin
Nucleoli not well resolved at this magnification
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows an increased population of small to medium-sized lymphoid cells with round to irregular nuclei, moderately condensed chromatin and scant to moderate deeply basophilic, agranular cytoplasm with frequent cytoplasmic protrusions. Occasional smudged cells are present, and red cells show crenation. Nucleoli are not well assessed at this magnification. Findings are consistent with T-cell prolymphocytic leukemia; flow cytometry and TCL1 immunostaining or cytogenetics for inv(14)/t(14;14) are recommended.

ddx.vs: CLL cells are small with clumped soccer-ball chromatin, scant pale cytoplasm and numerous smudge cells, and are CD5/CD23/CD200 positive B cells.
Sézary cells show cerebriform nuclear folds with pale cytoplasm and usually lose CD7, whereas T-PLL cells have basophilic blebbed cytoplasm and are CD7 bright.
LGL cells have abundant pale cytoplasm with azurophilic granules and a cytotoxic CD8/CD57 phenotype.
Hairy cells have pale grey-blue cytoplasm with fine circumferential hair-like projections and oval to bean-shaped nuclei, and are B cells with BRAF V600E.
